 Which Electric Vehicles Are The Most Recalled? 
 Written By: Jerry Reynolds 
 | Nov 18, 2026, 5:00:39 PM 
 Share: 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 The Tesla Model Y led a new ranking of electric vehicle safety recalls, with five campaigns covering more than 146,000 vehicles through Oct. 5. The Lucid Air finished second, followed by the Rivian R1S SUV and R1T pickup. One of the more interesting results, though, was Ford’s Mustang Mach-E. It ranked sixth with three recalls, yet those campaigns covered nearly 130,000 vehicles, second only to the Model Y among the top 10.
 The analysis comes from automotive research site REREV , which reviewed safety recall filing s with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration from Jan. 1 through Oct. 5, 2026. The study ranked 51 fully electric passenger models sold in the United States. It looked at recalls filed during that period, which can cover vehicles from multiple model years.
 REREV gave the number of campaigns 40% of a model’s score. It assigned 30% to the combined severity of the recalls and another 30% to how widely those problems affected vehicles, with more weight given to more serious defects. For example, a recall that tells owners to park outside because of a fire risk carries more weight than one for a missing label. The researchers also tracked owner complaints and federal investigations for context. The ranking itself came from the recall filings.
 The Top 10 EVs in REREV’s Safety Recall Ranking 
 The list shows each model’s recall count and the total number of U.S. vehicles covered across its campaigns. A vehicle included in two recalls can appear twice in that total.
 Tesla Model Y — 5 recalls, 146,042 vehicles
 Lucid Air — 4 recalls, 43,667 vehicles
 Rivian R1S — 4 recalls, 72,929 vehicles
 Rivian R1T — 4 recalls, 47,757 vehicles
 Hyundai Ioniq 5 — 4 recalls, 2,599 vehicles
 Ford Mustang Mach-E — 3 recalls, 129,413 vehicles
 Kia EV9 — 3 recalls, 21,738 vehicles
 Jeep Wagoneer S — 3 recalls, 23,831 vehicles
 Volvo EX30 — 3 recalls, 1,785 vehicles
 Tesla Model 3 — 3 recalls, 69,937 vehicles
 What Put These EVs on the List? 
 A delayed rearview camera image accounted for the biggest Model Y campaign in the study, covering about 113,000 vehicles. Another Model Y recall, for loose front suspension fasteners, covered just 19. Both counted as one campaign, which helps explain why REREV also considered how serious each problem was and how many vehicles it covered.
 The Lucid Air earned the highest combined severity score in the study. Its four campaigns included a fire risk tied to lighting-circuit software and a separate issue involving half-shaft bolts that could loosen. The Rivian R1S and R1T shared four campaigns involving the rearview camera display, rear suspension, front turn signals and seat belts. Two of the Hyundai Ioniq 5’s four campaigns involved battery short circuits that could cause a fire, and one carried a park-outside warning.
 REREV did not adjust the numbers for sales, so a model with more vehicles on the road has more vehicles that could be covered by a campaign. To estimate your odds of encountering a problem, you’d need to know how many of each model were on the road and how many individual vehicles were affected.
 If you’re shopping for a used EV, ask for the vehicle identification number and run it through NHTSA’s recall lookup. That tells you whether the specific car has an open safety recall. If one comes up, ask the seller whether the remedy is available and when the work can be done. If it’s a car you already own, follow any instructions in the recall notice and contact the dealer about the free remedy.
